parametrized_description: A random variable Z takes values 0, 1, ..., K with unknown probabilities p_0, p_1, ..., p_K. The first moment E[Z] = ExpectedZ and the second moment E[Z^2] = ExpectedZSquared are given. Find a probability distribution that provides a lower bound on the fourth moment E[Z^4] using linear programming.

K.description: Maximum value the random variable Z can take

Prob.description: Probability that Z takes value k

code.gurobipy: model.addConstr(quicksum(Prob[k] for k in range(K + 1)) == 1, name="ProbSum")

constraints.description: The first moment must equal ExpectedZ.

code.gurobipy: model.addConstr(quicksum(k * Prob[k] for k in range(K + 1)) == ExpectedZ, name="FirstMoment")

constraints.description: The second moment must equal ExpectedZSquared.

code.gurobipy: model.addConstr(quicksum(k**2 * Prob[k] for k in range(K + 1)) == ExpectedZSquared, name="SecondMoment")
model.addConstrs((Prob[k] >= 0 for k in range(K + 1)), name="NonNeg")

objective.description: Minimize the fourth moment E[Z^4] to find its lower bound.

code.gurobipy: model.setObjective(quicksum(k**4 * Prob[k] for k in range(K + 1)), GRB.MINIMIZE)
